views.summary: The routes that change a board, and what each hands the write to.

views.name: Reads and checks
views.summary: The routes that answer without changing a board: reads, health and the checks that run on request.

variants.name: Initial
variants.summary: The server's route handlers: what each one answers, and the store, lease, panes, renderer and history each reaches.

nodes.name: Board routes
nodes.responsibility: Mounts every board route and answers the reads: the family, the catalogue, one drawn view, the vault check

nodes.name: Board write routes
nodes.responsibility: The one write boundary: every route that changes a board goes through here
nodes.description: ADR 0023: the file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it. A write states the version it read, takes the board's lease, and is committed before it is answered.

nodes.name: Claim routes
nodes.responsibility: An agent's claim on a board, its release, and the person's override
nodes.description: ADR 0016 and ADR 0022: one writer at a time, visible in every pane showing the board, and the one control a person has over it is taking it back.

nodes.name: Rename route
nodes.responsibility: Renames a board or a variant as a write, and moves what the server keyed by the old name: its panes, its claim, what the agent said
nodes.description: TASK-281, ADR 0036. The old name stays a former name, so a pane or a command that still uses it reaches the board.

nodes.name: Discard route
nodes.responsibility: Lets a whole board go under the write's admission and lease, and tells every pane on it the board is gone
nodes.description: TASK-304.02: a board made only to be recorded, discarded by semantic record --discard.

nodes.name: Service routes
nodes.responsibility: Serves the page, and the health answer naming the archboard-server service, its pid and whether it runs the source on disk
nodes.description: The CLI signals a process for stop only when it both identifies as archboard-server and reports its own pid.

nodes.name: Code check route
nodes.responsibility: Runs the code check on request as checkout work, apart from the polled check

nodes.name: Locality route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's hotspots and change coupling over a period on request as checkout work; keeps each answer in memory until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves

nodes.name: Footprint route
nodes.responsibility: Answers one board's footprint on request as checkout work: reads the board and the proposal named, then asks the history lens for the parts a branch changed; keeps no answer

nodes.name: Live panes
nodes.responsibility: Keeps the panes on screen, their sockets and tabs, and board announcements live
nodes.description: Pane routes, Pane socket, Pane registry, Board announcements, Change feed, Tab session presence and Disk change watcher form this server subsystem. Board content stays on disk; the subsystem holds only screen and session state.

nodes.name: Application lifetime
nodes.responsibility: Boots and stops the server: the vault and loopback refusals, the pidfile, the ordered shutdown

nodes.name: Code findings memory
nodes.responsibility: What the last code pass found on each board and variant, in memory only
nodes.description: Each finished pass replaces the readings of the boards it read, with the version it read and when it ran; a cancelled pass changes nothing. GET /api/vault/code-findings answers from it alone, so a pane never starts a pass (ADR 0046).

nodes.name: Codex workbench
nodes.responsibility: Owns the private Codex child and bridges it to the panes

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Sends every board operation over HTTP and never writes a vault file itself

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads boards, says what each pane is showing, and writes nothing

nodes.name: Semantic board store
nodes.responsibility: The one place a board is read or written

nodes.name: Semantic renderer
nodes.responsibility: Draws one variant, view and theme as a self-contained document

nodes.name: Board lease
nodes.responsibility: One writer at a time per board: the lease file in the vault, an agent's claim, and news when the holder changes
nodes.description: ADR 0016. The lease lives beside the board, so every server on the vault sees the same exclusion.

nodes.name: History lens
nodes.responsibility: Maps checkout commits onto bound paths for behind and onto bound declarations for locality and footprint; labels path-wide fallback when a symbol cannot be resolved

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass over the files Git does not ignore in registered checkouts, through code facts: a bound symbol must be a definition, an anchor's symbol a definition or a use that supports its relationship (in the bound code of an end, of an evidence kind the relationship's kind accepts), and on a named draft a bound path must be in its checkout. Evidence between a board's bound parts comes from the code facts of every bound file, owned by the narrowest binding (a C, C++ or Objective-C file's part owns its pair): a run-time use through an import or include is a call, a type-only use an import. It joins an environment value that bound code reads with the compose service, Kubernetes workload or Terraform resource that runs that code (by its build, or a part drawn inside the part bound to it) and sets the value to another part's address: configured-path evidence. It reports the part code reaches with no relationship, and as information a relationship with no anchor whose accepted evidence runs only backwards or is missing (across a network hop, the side without evidence). For a container bound to a module it holds ADR 0044's interface to what the module exposes, and reads a Terraform module's pass-through variables and whether it is shallow. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there; references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. Kubernetes Service selectors and NetworkPolicies join workload-bound parts by labels, and a reference to a Service no part binds reaches the workloads it picks. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves, and a C use an include leads only to a declaration; the servers each checkout's registration holds decide which one runs there. It lists what it skipped and why. The header of src/shared/code-check/index.ts names each finding code and the task that added it, and skills/archboard/references/authoring.md says what each one asks of an author.

beats.heading: A read answers from the board family or a drawing made here
beats.body: Board routes reads the family from the store and draws a selected view with the renderer. The browser holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this answered.

beats.heading: Every change passes the write routes and the board's lease
beats.body: Board write routes states the version it read, writes through the store under the board's lease, and announces the accepted write to the panes. Rename and discard hand their writes to it, and the file is committed before any of them answers.

beats.heading: A claim, a rename and a discard move more than the board
beats.body: Claim routes takes, releases or takes back the claim in the lease, rename carries the claim and the panes to the new name, and discard tells every pane the board is gone.

beats.heading: A check runs on request, as work on the checkout
beats.body: The code check route keeps what a finished pass found. The locality route keeps each answer until a board version or a checkout HEAD moves. The footprint route keeps none.
